A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey-based research. Their complete text, six figures, table, questionnaire, and language appendix support reliable comparison despite rewriting, renumbering, and layout changes.

before.justification: v5 reports original quantitative and qualitative analysis of 81 survey responses, including findings on motivations, resource limitations, and credit attribution in Section 4.

after.justification: v6 retains the original analysis of 81 survey responses and its quantitative and qualitative findings in Section 4 and Figures 3–6.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an algorithm or model architecture. The survey approach remains unchanged; expanded ethical recommendations do not introduce an algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both examine the same population and research-practice questions across more than 70 named languages. The language list is identical after matching v5 Appendix A.2 to v6 Appendix B.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing methods or baselines. Newly cited studies support discussion and recommendations rather than comparative experiments.

E3.justification: The June–October 2024 recruitment period, recruitment channels, 81-response sample, questionnaire, and quantitative/qualitative analysis procedures are retained. Appendix questionnaire edits are wording changes, not changes to questions or response options.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, or separate supplementary analyses are introduced. The ablation and error-analysis activities newly mentioned in Section 5.2 are suggestions for contributors, not studies performed in this work.

E5.justification: Both report descriptive frequencies without confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run procedures. Figure 5 converts the existing counts into equivalent percentages without introducing a new statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 3 corrects incentive values and rankings: for example, NLP/CL/ML interest changes from approximately 78% to 68%, and LLM research from approximately 25% to 59%, matching the already-stated Section 4.2 percentages. Other quantitative distributions are retained. Section 5.1 adds more specific reports of undeserved first authorship and emotional manipulation involving both small groups and Big Tech.

T1.justification: Neither version contains formal mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorems, or proofs. The added ethical concepts and recommendations are conceptual discussion rather than mathematical theory.

C1.justification: v6 removes the conclusion's categorical claim that this is the first work documenting NLP researchers' and workers' experiences. The central contribution—survey-based findings and recommendations for culturally appropriate resources and fair treatment of workers—remains.

C2.justification: v6 extends the existing ethical discussion with concrete coauthorship criteria in Section 5.2, consent and deontological concerns about Indigenous texts in Section 5.5, and positionality guidance in new Section 5.6. It also adds the authors' positionality statement. The selection-bias limitation remains acknowledged.

D1.justification: Recruitment details, the manual response-processing description, the full questionnaire, and confidentiality disclosures are retained. No new analysis implementation details, code availability, or survey-data access instructions are supplied.

R1.justification: v6 adds supporting works on dataset construction, Big Tech, cultural heterogeneity, and the authors' previous annotation projects, including Yu et al. (2022), Abdalla et al. (2023), Keleg (2025), Ousidhoum et al. (2024), and Muhammad et al. (2025). It softens novelty positioning while retaining the existing relationship to participatory research.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, survey description, findings prose, and recommendations undergo extensive rewriting. Section 5.2 is reorganized into compensation and coauthorship guidance, new sections address positionality, and the appendices are relabeled A and B. This substantially revises the exposition beyond adding content.

P2.justification: All four quantitative charts are redrawn: Figures 3–4 receive larger, wrapped horizontal labels; Figure 5 replaces a stacked count bar with a percentage-labeled pie; and Figure 6 changes proportions, labels, and styling. Captions gain emphasis, Table 1 moves from page 4 to page 3, and the appendix layout changes.

improvement.justification: v6 fixes Figure 3's disagreement with the existing incentive percentages, improves chart legibility, and makes authorship and positionality guidance more actionable. The author positionality statement and removal of the categorical novelty claim improve transparency and calibration. These are clear but limited gains; Figure 5's replacement of raw counts with percentages makes its response denominator less explicit.
